test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is an efficient way to organise files on a computer?

options.text: Create different folders based on categories of files
Rename all files with random characters
Keep all files in the same folder
Store all files in the Recycle Bin

solution:
The correct answer is __**Create different folders based on categories of files**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Efficient file organization:** Creating different folders based on categories of files is an effective way to manage data. It helps in easy retrieval and prevents clutter.
 
• **Categories based on file types:** Files can be grouped under specific categories such as **documents, images, videos, spreadsheets, and software**. This categorization ensures logical arrangement and prevents misplacement.
 
• **Enhanced productivity:** Organizing files into folders reduces the time spent searching for files, thereby increasing efficiency and saving valuable time. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Logical structure:** A well-maintained folder system encourages a logical structure for data, allowing users to intuitively navigate through their files without confusion.
 
• **Backup and synchronization:** Files organized into folders can be easily backed up or synchronized with cloud storage systems like **Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive**. This ensures data safety and accessibility.
 
• **Scalability:** As the volume of data increases, a folder structure can scale accordingly by adding subfolders within categories. For example, within a "Documents" folder, you can create subfolders like "Work," "Personal," or "Projects." *Hence, this is a highly effective method.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of file organization:**

 
 
• Proper file organization ensures **data security**, minimizes redundancy, and enhances accessibility to important files.
 
• It also reduces the risk of losing files and makes collaborative work easier, especially in a professional setting.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of folder-based categorization:**
 
 
• It allows individuals to sort files based on **priority, date, or relevance**. For example, project files can be grouped separately from personal files.
 
• **Search and retrieval:** Organizing files helps users quickly locate specific files using search functions or folder navigation.
 
• **Examples:** In professional environments, folders named "Invoices," "Reports," and "Meeting Notes" are commonly used to organize work-related files.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 2:** Renaming all files with random characters is not practical, as it makes file identification difficult and retrieval confusing. This method is inefficient.
 
• **Option 3:** Keeping all files in the same folder leads to clutter, making it harder to locate specific files. It is not recommended for effective organization.
 
• **Option 4:** Storing files in the Recycle Bin is illogical as it is meant for discarded items. Files in the Recycle Bin are often deleted permanently, making this option incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Best practices:** Always name folders descriptively and use consistent naming conventions to avoid confusion. Regularly review and clean up folders to remove outdated or unnecessary files.
